messages.content: Java is a programming language created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems in 1995. It was designed to address some of the issues associated with C and C++, particularly platform dependence and memory management. Java compiles into "bytecode" which can run on any device that has a Java Virtual Machine (JVM) installed, making it "Write Once, Run Anywhere." The JVM also includes automatic garbage collection, eliminating the need for manual memory management and reducing common bugs in C/C++. Java is strictly object-oriented, enforcing a rigid, organized structure with everything belonging to a class or object. Primary use cases include enterprise-level backend systems (such as banking software and massive web servers), native Android mobile applications, and large-scale data processing tools. The vibe of using Java is similar to driving a modern, high-end automatic SUV - it's safe, has built-in guardrails, and can navigate various terrains, but you cannot open the hood and tweak the engine while driving.
